source_scope.extraction: Exact source from namespace aph::comms through immediately before void bag(int gems), unchanged; source-bound functions are compiled and run against thin host mocks.

fixture_code.historical_runner_pin_note: The archived v2 runner was reconstructed from v1 plus the v2 changes after its original working copy was superseded; it reproduces the archived v2 generated C++ byte-for-byte and passes the 13 v2 scenarios.

scenarios.name: round-765-positive-replacement
scenarios.details: Fixture Vesper uses actual basic attack range 3 plus ready dash bonus 2 plus three pursuit steps; contact is Chebyshev distance 6. Replacement sets the marker without advancing ordinary generation and preserves newly fresh unrelated bag/camp/claim fields.

scenarios.name: second-replacement-marker
scenarios.details: After first replacement, fixture moves the sender away and exposes a different current, otherwise eligible contact; second same-round send leaves bits unchanged, so the marker—not identical-payload equality—blocks another replacement.

scenarios.name: normal-publication-freshness-and-wrap
scenarios.details: Exact production writer helper and expect/receive recognize same contact across alternating parity, generation wraps after four. Additional normal-write scenario exercises send() publishing unchanged visible contact on consecutive turns.

scenarios.name: nonconsecutive-send-marker-0
scenarios.details: After a missed-turn gap, send() does not mutate stale current-parity contact/generation; next healthy consecutive turn publishes and advances generation.

scenarios.name: nonconsecutive-send-marker-1
scenarios.details: Same no-refresh assertion with replacement marker already set.

limitations: Thin mocks model World, shared memory, visible records, and actor observations; no WASI/native SDK integration or real engine scheduling.
The fixture exercises production functions but not caller-side dispatch.
compiler_warnings: Two harmless unused mock constants: capture_time and cambc::error_code::ok.
